name: Atlas service account client ID
description: The Client ID of an Atlas service account: mdb_sa_id_ followed by 24 hexadecimal characters of either case, documented as a schema pattern. It is the username-like half of the pair whose other half is the service account secret, so it sits beside the secret in scripts and configuration. The pages read do not say whether it may be exposed, so its non-secret status is not asserted here, only that it is a separate component from the secret and has its own documented shape.

sources.supports: clientId: 'The Client ID of the Service Account', pattern ^mdb_sa_id_[a-fA-F\d]{24}$
Each service account has a client ID and a rotatable secret that function as a username and a password for creating access tokens.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Class is unresolved because the cited pages document the shape and role but contain no statement about whether the Client ID is safe to expose.
